When a piece of state or a decision is already derivable from an existing canonical source, every layer of the stack must consume that source rather than re-implementing its own version of the rule. Divergent implementations drift: a Git handoff tool picked a remote with "current branch's remote, else origin" while the workspace manifest used "origin, else first remote," so the confirmation screen and the actual push could silently target different repositories; a desktop schema added a `providerConfigured` flag that duplicated readiness already available from the shared provider catalog, forcing extra caching/sync work to keep the two in agreement. Prefer extending the shared contract (e.g. `GatewayProviderMetadata.apiKeyOptional` surfaced as `ProviderAuthInfo.apiKeyOptional`) over adding a parallel field that must be kept in sync by hand, and move repository/remote validation into the shared core module rather than duplicating bespoke checks in each host.

This consistency requirement also applies at the request/response boundary itself:
- If you add a field to a request/input type, trace it through every place the matching response/event is constructed so it is actually returned — a field that goes in but never comes back out is a trap for the next integrator (e.g. `displayPrompt` accepted on input but dropped from the `pending_prompt_submitted` event projections).
- Never repurpose an existing header/field to carry different semantics while keeping its old name — if `X-Task-ID` is going to carry a `ulid` instead of a task id, either keep sending the task id, rename the header, or send both as distinct fields, so the contract stays unambiguous to any consumer.

Before merging a new or changed contract, grep for all producers and consumers of the same concept and confirm there is exactly one authoritative implementation/schema for it.
